supports: Targeted deregulation to keep jobs and investment in New York City
positions.quote: Support strategic, common-sense deregulation to allow industry and innovation to flourish and combat the mass exodus of jobs, opportunity, investment, and capital out of New York City
positions.impact: She would vote to reduce federal business regulations. As one of 435 House members, they would vote and push for this in Congress; it would only become law with majorities in both chambers and the President's signature.

supports: Lowering the federal income tax on W-2 wages
positions.quote: Protect the Paycheck – allow people to keep more of what they earn by reducing the federal income tax on W-2 wages.
positions.impact: Salaried and hourly workers would pay less federal income tax under her proposal. As one of 435 House members, they would vote and push for this in Congress; it would only become law with majorities in both chambers and the President's signature.

positions.quote: Reintroduce competition into the healthcare marketplace and enhance price transparency to ensure the system works for patients and providers, not just the insurance companies
positions.impact: Patients could see more published prices for care and more insurance options. As one of 435 House members, they would vote and push for this in Congress; it would only become law with majorities in both chambers and the President's signature.

supports: A pro-safety, pro-community law enforcement agenda
positions.quote: Prioritize the safety and security of New Yorkers and their livelihoods through a pro-safety, pro-community law enforcement agenda
positions.impact: Expect support for federal funding for police. Day-to-day policing is run by the NYPD.

supports: Standing with New York City's Jewish community and with Israel
positions.quote: Unapologetically stand with the Jewish community of New York City and our ally Israel
positions.impact: She would likely vote for continued U.S. support for Israel. As one of 435 House members, they would vote and push for this in Congress; it would only become law with majorities in both chambers and the President's signature.
